newsitem.title: ITALY: Berlusconi, Craxi graft trial adjourned to Dec 9.
newsitem.headline: Berlusconi, Craxi graft trial adjourned to Dec 9.

text.p: A trial of former Italian prime ministers Silvio Berlusconi and Bettino Craxi for corruption formally opened on Thursday but was immediately adjourned until December 9, court sources said.

Berlusconi, billionaire boss of the Fininvest media empire, is accused of acquiescing in payments by his company of 10 billion lire ($6.5 million) alleged to have been channelled to Craxi through a Fininvest-linked off-shore company, All Iberian, and various Swiss bank accounts.

Berlusconi is charged with false accounting and illegal financing of political parties along with 11 others, including self-exiled ex-Socialist party leader Craxi. None of the defendants turned up for the hearing.
Presiding judge Marco Ghezzi granted the defence's request for an adjournment to have time to examine documents supplied by auditors Arthur Andersen relating to Fininvest's accounts.
The court also decided that a recording of the trial could be broadcast, but not live, by Italian RAI state television.
Berlusconi, prime minister for seven stormy months in 1994, is already on trial in Milan on a separate charge of alleged complicity in the payment of Fininvest bribes to tax inspectors.
Craxi, charged with receiving the illegal All Iberian cash, lives in Tunisia and says he is too ill to return to Italy.
Italy's highest court of appeal last week confirmed a five and a half year prison sentence against Craxi for illegal party financing, meaning he would go to jail if he ever returned here.
Premier from 1983 to 1987, Craxi has appeals pending against three other court convictions for which he has been sentenced to jail terms totalling a further 20 years and three months.
